=======================================
Using declarations are declarations, not assignments
=======================================

using file = getFile();
await using resource = getResource();
using a = 1, b = 2;

---

(program
  (using_declaration
    (variable_declarator
      name: (identifier)
      value: (call_expression
        function: (identifier)
        arguments: (arguments))))
  (using_declaration
    (variable_declarator
      name: (identifier)
      value: (call_expression
        function: (identifier)
        arguments: (arguments))))
  (using_declaration
    (variable_declarator
      name: (identifier)
      value: (number))
    (variable_declarator
      name: (identifier)
      value: (number))))

=======================================
Using declarations with type annotations
=======================================

using file: Disposable = getFile();
await using resource: AsyncDisposable = getResource();

---

(program
  (using_declaration
    (variable_declarator
      name: (identifier)
      type: (type_annotation
        (type_identifier))
      value: (call_expression
        function: (identifier)
        arguments: (arguments))))
  (using_declaration
    (variable_declarator
      name: (identifier)
      type: (type_annotation
        (type_identifier))
      value: (call_expression
        function: (identifier)
        arguments: (arguments)))))

=======================================
Using declarations in for-of heads
=======================================

for (using r of xs) {}
for (await using r of xs) {}
for await (await using r of xs) {}

---

(program
  (for_in_statement
    left: (identifier)
    right: (identifier)
    body: (statement_block))
  (for_in_statement
    left: (identifier)
    right: (identifier)
    body: (statement_block))
  (for_in_statement
    left: (identifier)
    right: (identifier)
    body: (statement_block)))

=======================================
Using declarations in classic for heads
=======================================

for (using d1 = open(), d2 = null;;) {}

---

(program
  (for_statement
    initializer: (using_declaration
      (variable_declarator
        name: (identifier)
        value: (call_expression
          function: (identifier)
          arguments: (arguments)))
      (variable_declarator
        name: (identifier)
        value: (null)))
    condition: (empty_statement)
    body: (statement_block)))

=======================================
Using declaration inside a function body
=======================================

function f() {
  using h = open();
  await using k = openAsync();
  return h;
}

---

(program
  (function_declaration
    name: (identifier)
    parameters: (formal_parameters)
    body: (statement_block
      (using_declaration
        (variable_declarator
          name: (identifier)
          value: (call_expression
            function: (identifier)
            arguments: (arguments))))
      (using_declaration
        (variable_declarator
          name: (identifier)
          value: (call_expression
            function: (identifier)
            arguments: (arguments))))
      (return_statement
        (identifier)))))

=======================================
Using is still an identifier in an ordinary binary expression
=======================================

const z = using + 1;

---

(program
  (lexical_declaration
    (variable_declarator
      name: (identifier)
      value: (binary_expression
        left: (identifier)
        right: (number)))))
